question: how do i add my parent as an authorized user so they can pay my bill

question: Should I take out a private loan or just work more hours to cover the gap this semester? i have like $2k left
answer:
Financial Aid: grants do not have to be repaid; loans must be repaid; and Federal Work-Study offers a chance to earn money at an on- or off-campus job [3]. Subsidized Federal Direct loans have interest paid by the Federal government while you are in school; unsubsidized loan interest accrues while you are in school. Work-study requires you to work, pays every two weeks, and is not subtracted from your bill. For questions, contact the Office of Financial Aid at (201) 684-7549 or finaid@ramapo.edu [1].

On-Campus Employment for Students: Federal work-study and student aide positions are posted on Handshake, where students can view and apply directly to hiring units [4].
1. The supervisor describes the position and decides whether to offer it. The discussion should cover the job description and skill compatibility; starting date; weekly hours that do not conflict with classes; schedule changes for mid-terms, exams and breaks; conduct and dress; salary; responsibility for college facilities and equipment; confidentiality; timekeeping; and punctuality and attendance.
2. If you accept an offer, you and the supervisor sign an employment form with the beginning work date, salary, etc. Return all copies of the required paperwork (New hire packet, W-4 Form and I-9 Form) to the Student Assistant Program Office in Room D-119 [4].

Student Accounts: The Ramapo Tuition Payment Plan (RTPP) spreads tuition payments over installments; there are two Fall and Spring options and a Summer plan [6]. All students are encouraged to fill out the FAFSA; the Ramapo School Code is 009344. After eligibility is determined, you can work with a Financial aid counselor to potentially find resources for a remaining balance [6]. For Parent PLUS or alternative loans, see https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/wp-content/uploads/sites/14/2024/02/Parent-Private-Loan-Tip-Sheet-2024.pdf and explore options or apply at https://www.elmselect.com/v4/; counselors are available at finaid@ramapo.edu [6].

Admissions: Freshmen can borrow up to $5,500, sophomores $6,500, and juniors and seniors $7,500 through the Direct Loan program; alternative loans from private lenders are also available [9].

question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress
answer:
A student may NOT withdraw from a course after the published deadline [3]. Deadlines are posted on the Academic Calendar: https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/ [3]. The pages describe a possible late administrative withdrawal under extraordinary circumstances: ordinarily, apply before the end of the semester; explain why standard withdrawal procedures could not be followed, state the term, and provide appropriate documentation. It typically results in W grades for all courses in that term; ordinarily, only one term per appeal [5]. The provided page text does not give the application form or submission instructions. The Registrar says an approved course withdrawal after the refund period records a W and gives no refund [3]; that is not permission to withdraw after the deadline.

Withdrawing may affect financial aid and satisfactory progress toward graduation [1]. For a withdrawal after the refund period, federal aid should not be affected if you remain enrolled in 6 or more credits; NJ State aid requires full-time enrollment when aid is fully disbursed [10]. SAP eligibility is reviewed annually after spring; students who do not meet its standards lose financial aid eligibility [7]. These pages do not establish whether your particular course withdrawal will affect your aid or SAP status. Contact Financial Aid to discuss your circumstances: finaid@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7549, E-210 [10].

Contact the Registrar about the deadline or withdrawal process: reg@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7695, D-224 [3].

question: I got a credit balance on my student account after my aid posted, how do I get that money sent to me? Do I need to sign up for direct deposit or does it just get mailed?
answer:
Student Accounts handles credit-balance refunds. Unless you specify otherwise, the College issues a paper check, mailed to your billing/permanent address; it will not go to a campus mailbox and cannot be picked up at Student Accounts. Direct deposit is optional and free. [1]

To sign up: [3]
1. Log into RCNJ Experience: https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/
2. Locate the Student Account Info card; click Bill & Payment Suite, then Electronic Refunds on the right under My Profile Setup.
3. Enroll in Two-Step Verification (skip if previously completed): in My Profile, click Security Settings, select a passcode method (text message, email or Google Authentication), click Send Code, enter the passcode and click Verify.
4. Click Payment Profile; edit an existing saved Payment Method or create a new one. Check the box in Refund Option to designate it as the direct-deposit refund account.

An eligible refund is expected within one to two weeks of submitting the application. [2] Title IV aid overpayments resulting in a credit balance of $1.00 or greater are refunded; non-Title IV financial aid has a $5.00 threshold. [1] The fastest way to receive a refund is direct deposit. [7]

Questions: Student Accounts, studentaccts@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7495; D-Wing, First Floor. [1, 2]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/deposits/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit-questions-answers/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/scholarships/faqs/)

question: im a transfer student and i commute, how do i get a parking permit and where do i park
answer:

Section 10 directs you to the RCNJ Parking Permits portal: select permit type; complete contact information and click “Save/Update Person,” then “Continue”; enter vehicle information; review and continue; then print or save the Registration Filed page with your request number. question: how do i apply to graduate? i'm a senior finishing in december
answer:
The Registrar says all candidates must apply. [3]

1. Make an appointment with your advisor to confirm you are ready to apply. Your advisor will remove your graduation hold, giving you access to the online application. Your degree audit must have all areas satisfied; if it needs an adjustment, email your advisor or convener before applying. The advisor/convener will contact your dean with recommended adjustments. [2]
2. Complete the online Graduation Application. The Registrar’s Graduation / Commencement page is https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/. [1,2]
3. The page’s online instructions say to log on to Experience Webapp at https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/, locate “Student Self-Service Card,” click “Open Student Dashboard,” select “Student Profile,” select the Spring term with the down arrow, click “Application to Graduate,” fill in the information and submit. [4] Note: the page gives “Spring term” for this step, while the deadline table lists Fall as the term with a November 6 deadline; the pages differ on which term to select. [4,13]

For a December finish, the pages list Fall graduation applications as available June 1 to November 6, with a November 6 deadline; official conferral is January 22, 2027. The FAQ also gives January graduates an apply-until date of November 6. [9,13] Late applicants should use the double major application. [8]

Contact the Registrar at reg@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7695, D-224, with questions. [2,13]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/)

question: my roommate keeps having his girlfriend sleep over like 5 nights a week. is there a guest policy and who do i talk to about it
answer:
Housing & Residence Life’s guest policy says guests may not move from host to host to stay on campus more than three (3) nights. It does not specify in the supplied text a limit for a guest staying with the same host, so I can’t verify whether five nights a week in your situation violates the policy. Roommates have the right to sleep without unnecessary disturbances and to host guests only while respecting others’ rights and following guest policies. [1,3,8]

Talk with your roommate about your concerns. You can contact your Resident Assistant to facilitate a roommate contract. If someone violates that contract, staff in the hall/area office must receive a formal complaint before they can act. [1,3]

Housing & Residence Life: reslife@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7461. [1,3]

question: What do I need to do to move out of my dorm when I graduate? is there a checkout process and what happens if I'm late
answer:
Housing & Residence Life handles residence-hall check-out. Contact reslife@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7461; the checklist also says to contact your RA or Hall office before check-out. [1]

For spring end-of-year check-out:
1. Follow the [check-out checklist](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/check-out-checklist/). Remove trash and recyclables, personal items and property; leave the College refrigerator on at level 5; set the thermostat to auto, low, at 70°F; clean thoroughly; close blinds, lock windows, turn off lights, close the door, empty your campus mailbox, update correspondents with your new mailing address, and leave drawers open. [1]
2. Leave by the check-out deadline based on your last exam schedule. [1] The pages here don’t give your graduating term’s specific deadline; check with Housing & Residence Life.
3. Provide your own cart or dolly if needed; the College won’t provide moving equipment. Items left behind will be discarded, and fines may apply. [2] Final inspections happen after residents vacate; occupants should prepare the room, suite, or apartment together. Failed inspections or prohibited items may be billed. [9] The College is not responsible for belongings left behind. [9]

If you need to stay past the designated date and time, complete the [Check-Out Extension Request process](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/). Extensions won’t be granted for non-academic reasons, including unavailable/late transportation or off-campus employment; approved extensions don’t allow guests. [6] Not vacating as required may result in a $75 improper check-out fine. [2] The fines page says failure to follow posted check-out times is $75. [4] For excessive garbage, section 1 says fines start at $25 per bundle, while section 4 says $25 per bag; the pages differ. [1][4]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/check-out-checklist/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/spring-check-out/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/spring-check-out/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/spring-check-out/)

question: how do i get a work study job on campus? i have it in my aid package but idk where to apply
answer:
The On-Campus Employment for Students office says to register on Handshake to view open positions, search with keyword “RCNJ,” and follow the instructions in each posting; apply directly to the hiring unit and contact the listed supervisor. [1][5][6] All federal work-study and student aide positions are posted on Handshake: ramapo.joinhandshake.com. [1][5] Students awarded Federal Work-Study as part of their financial aid package receive priority for Student Assistant positions. [6]
If you’re offered a position and accept it, you and your supervisor sign an employment form with your beginning work date and salary. Return all copies of the required paperwork—the New hire packet, W-4 Form and I-9 Form—to the Student Assistant Program Office, Room D-119. [1]
For help, contact On-Campus Employment for Students at sap@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7654, Room D-119. [1]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/on-campus-employment/policies-and-procedures/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/on-campus-employment/faqs/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/on-campus-employment/)
